query: Which monotone neural scalarizer architectures and parameterizations (positive-weight layers, monotone networks, ICNNs or partially-ordered nets) guarantee preservation of preference ordering, and how are constraints enforced during training?

response.query: Which monotone neural scalarizer architectures and parameterizations (positive-weight layers, monotone networks, ICNNs or partially-ordered nets) guarantee preservation of preference ordering, and how are constraints enforced during training?
response.answer: Monotone neural networks with positive-weight layers and ICNNs enforce monotonicity through training loss penalties. Constraints are directly incorporated into the loss function to ensure preference ordering is preserved.

results.title: Size and depth of monotone neural networks: interpolation and approximation
results.content: We will mainly be interested in expressiveness, the ability to approximate monotone functions, and interpolate monotone data sets with monotone neural networks of constant depth. Namely, we give a construction of a smooth monotone function with a Lipschitz constant such that can be approximated within an additive error of by a general neural network with neurons. Now we show that given a Boolean circuit to compute a given function , we can construct a general (not necessarily monotone) threshold network of comparable size to approximate arbitrarily well. It is reasonable to expect that one could use our machinery to demonstrate monotone real functions that can be computed by a bounded depth circuit yet require super polynomial size to be approximated by monotone networks.
